question.text: What will voter turnout be in Spain's November 29, 2026 general election?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the official nationwide turnout (participación) in the November 29, 2026 election to the Congress of Deputies, defined as total ballots cast divided by the total registered electorate including voters resident abroad (CERA), according to credible sources such as the Ministry of the Interior at infoelectoral.interior.gob.es or by the Junta Electoral Central. The latest figure published as of December 31, 2026 is used.
question.fine_print: This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46270) which opened on 2026-10-26 17:00:00. This question will resolve based on the resolution criteria and fine print of the linked original question. However, if this question would resolve differently than the original question, then this question will be annulled. Additionally, if the original question's resolution could have been known before this question opened, then this question will be annulled.

research:
Every bullet below carries its dated source. Kalshi conversions use the 38,730,187 electorate (about 38.73M).

## 1. Resolution source
- Fixed reference: the Interior Ministry's results site, [infoelectoral.interior.gob.es](https://infoelectoral.interior.gob.es), reports turnout as total ballots cast divided by the full electorate, including voters resident abroad (CERA). For 23 July 2023 that figure was 66.59%. The election-night count excludes CERA, so it runs about 3.8 points higher: about 70.4% in 2023. Most media and pollsters who cite "70%/71% in 2023" mean that resident-only figure. This is the most important trap for this question. I did not fetch the ministry page; no 2026 results exist yet.
- 2026-11-04: The final electoral roll has 38,730,187 voters: 35,953,542 resident and 2,776,645 CERA (about 7.2%), across 61,033 polling stations. [La Región](https://www.laregion.es/comarca-de-ourense/galicia-aporta-2-7-38-7-millones-electores-totales-espana_1_20261104-4478317.html). Statistics institute (INE) figures reported by Antena 3 are slightly different: 38,728,356 total, 2,769,645 CERA, and 1.6M first-time voters. [Antena3](https://www.antena3.com/noticias/espana/quien-tiene-derecho-votar-elecciones-generales_202611046aeb1043d3bddc0868a4b00b.html)
- CERA is up 18% since 2023. [RTVE](https://www.rtve.es/noticias/20261104/elecciones-2026-como-votar-desde-extranjero-voto-cera/17297726.shtml). CERA turnout is usually very low (roughly 10%), so a bigger CERA share pulls the headline figure down. My rough conversion: official turnout ≈ 0.928 × resident turnout + 0.7 points.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. Voting is on 29 November; CERA votes are counted a few days later. The campaign starts 13 November.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03/04: Requests for postal votes close 19 November. [ABC](https://www.abc.es/espana/andalucia/voto-correo-elecciones-generales-29n-dia-puede-20261103165227-nts.html). Polling-station staff are being drawn by lot 31 October to 4 November. [Antena3](https://www.antena3.com/noticias/espana/cuando-sabe-toca-formar-parte-mesa-electoral-elecciones-fechas-plazos-como-reclamar_202611046aead8084196933d7ed00466.html)
- 2026-10-27: NC Report for La Razón (fieldwork 22-24 Oct) puts turnout among residents in Spain at 68.43%, below "71% in 2023". It projects 50% abstention among 18-29 year olds. Converted, that is about 64.2% on the official measure. [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/10/27/asi-estan-las-encuestas-para-el-29-de-noviembre-pp-y-vox-mantienen-la-mayoria-absoluta-el-psoe-gana-terreno-y-la-izquierda-fragmentada-no-logra-remontar/). Polls still show a PP plus Vox majority.
- 2026-10-17: Michavila (GAD3) and Iván Redondo expect one of the highest turnouts of the democratic era. A search summary attributes 76-77% to Michavila, compared with "70% in 2023", so likely resident-only; I could not confirm the number behind the paywall. That converts to about 71-72%. Metroscopia sees more intent to vote in both blocs. 40dB finds the left slightly less mobilised. [infoLibre](https://www.infolibre.es/politica/expertos-anticipan-participacion-record-29n-discrepan-recortar-derecha_1_2238515.html)
- Undated, October: Demócrata says turnout "points to 74%", 3.6 points above 23 July 2023, so a resident-only basis. That converts to about 69.4%. I got a 403 error and could not verify it. [Demócrata](https://www.democrata.es/en/general-elections-spain/the-participation-of-29-n-points-to-74-it-would-be-the-highest-in-general-election-since-2004/)
- 2026-10-14: The CIS October barometer has PSOE 34%, PP 22.2%, Vox 17.1%. [El Diario de Madrid](https://www.eldiariodemadrid.es/articulo/politica/encuesta-cis-octubre-2026-psoe-pp-vox-elecciones-generales-29-noviembre/20261014135517144139.html). I did not find a CIS turnout estimate. Its pre-election macro-survey (study 3584, 45,000 interviews) is pending. [Demócrata](https://www.democrata.es/en/general-elections-spain/the-undecided-of-29n-the-cis-reveals-where-they-are/)
- 2026-10-05: Sánchez dissolved the Cortes after two housing decrees were defeated in Congress. The election comes about 9 months early. [Cronista](https://www.cronista.com/internacionales/pedro-sanchez-adelanta-las-elecciones-en-espana-tras-el-fracaso-de-sus-leyes-para-regular-la-vivienda/)

## 4. Base rates
- Recent official figures (CERA included): 2011 68.94%, 2015 69.67%, 2016 66.48%, Apr 2019 71.76%, Nov 2019 66.23%, 2023 66.59%. The 1977-2023 mean is about 72.6%; the background's "68%" average looks understated.
- Since 2011 the range is 66.2-71.8%, and the last three elections were all near 66-67%.
- Change between consecutive elections: median about 3 points, maximum about 9.
- November elections: 2011 68.94%, 2019 66.23%.
- High turnout tends to come in polarised "change" elections (1982, 1996, 2004, April 2019), which is the argument for turnout above 70%.
- Structural drag: a larger CERA share reduces the headline figure by about 0.3 points compared with 2023, all else equal.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi turnout market (2026-11-04), priced in vote counts. Approximate implied turnout: 25.0M (64.5%) 88% yes; 25.5M (65.8%) 73%; 26.0M (67.1%) 61%; 26.5M (68.4%) 45%; 27.0M (69.7%) 29%; 27.5M (71.0%) 19%; 28.0M (72.3%) 10%. The implied median is about 26.4M, roughly 68.2% if the contract counts CERA ballots. I did not verify the contract's exact definition.
- Polymarket (2026-11-04): <62% 4%; 62-64% 7.5%; 64-66% 18%; 66-68% 15.5%; 68-70% 27%; 70%+ 35.5%. These sum to about 108%, which suggests a median near 68-69%. Polymarket may resolve on the election-night resident-only figure, which would make it upward-biased against this question. Check its rules.
- Related markets: Polymarket gives PP 87% to win. Kalshi's median is roughly 135 PP seats and roughly 65-70 Vox seats.
- No Manifold market or academic forecast found.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 13-27 November: the campaign, with debates and La Séptima's daily tracking polls. [elDiario.es](https://eldiario.es/vertele/noticias/septima-ofrecera-encuestas-diarias-29n-gran-baza-arranque-cambiar-campana-electoral_1_13637270.html)
- The CIS pre-election survey is due, probably mid-November.
- 19 November: deadline for postal vote requests. Postal-vote demand is a useful early signal.
- 29 November: election night (resident-only turnout, plus intraday turnout readings at 14:00 and 18:00). Late-November weather may matter.
- About 2-4 December: CERA ballots counted, producing the CERA-inclusive figure that decides this question. Final scrutiny follows.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-04: Infoelectoral (infoelectoral.interior.gob.es) only has past elections. No 2026 turnout figure exists yet, and none can until after the vote on November 29. I did not fetch the site directly.
- 2026-11-04: The final Electoral Census Office lists give 38,730,187 voters: 35,953,542 resident in Spain and 2,776,645 abroad (CERA), across 61,033 polling stations. [La Región](https://www.laregion.es/comarca-de-ourense/galicia-aporta-2-7-38-7-millones-electores-totales-espana_1_20261104-4478317.html). Earlier INE figures were 38,728,356 in total, with 2,769,645 abroad. [Antena 3](https://www.antena3.com/noticias/espana/quien-tiene-derecho-votar-elecciones-generales_202611046aeb1043d3bddc0868a4b00b.html)
- **Definition trap:** on election night, Interior reports turnout among resident voters only. In 2023 that figure was about 70.4%. The figure that counts here includes CERA and only comes out after the final count (the scrutiny), which is 66.59% for 2023. The two can differ by about 4 points.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The election is 25 days away.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: The CERA census is 2,769,645, up 18% on 2023. Ballot papers are sent to voters abroad automatically. [RTVE](https://www.rtve.es/noticias/20261104/elecciones-2026-como-votar-desde-extranjero-voto-cera/17297726.shtml)
- 2026-11-04: There are 1,615,127 first-time voters. [Antena 3](https://www.antena3.com/noticias/espana/quien-tiene-derecho-votar-elecciones-generales_202611046aeb1043d3bddc0868a4b00b.html)
- 2026-11-03: The deadline to request a postal vote is November 19. [ABC](https://www.abc.es/espana/andalucia/voto-correo-elecciones-generales-29n-dia-puede-20261103165227-nts.html)
- 2026-10-25: The October polling average excluding the CIS is PP 32.0%, PSOE 26.4%, Vox 18.8%, Sumar/FA 6.0%. PP+Vox are projected at 198 to 212 seats. No turnout estimates are published. [El Debate](https://www.eldebate.com/espana/20261025/dicen-ultimas-encuestas-sobre-elecciones-generales-29-noviembre-cns_472138.html)
- 2026-10-14: The CIS October barometer has PSOE 34.0%, PP 22.2%, Vox 17.1%. The CIS is planning a 45,000-interview pre-election survey. [El Diario de Madrid](https://www.eldiariodemadrid.es/articulo/politica/encuesta-cis-octubre-2026-psoe-pp-vox-elecciones-generales-29-noviembre/20261014135517144139.html), [The Objective](https://theobjective.com/espana/2026-10-14/cis-macroencuesta-45000-entrevistas-elecciones-29n/). Demócrata re-ran the CIS numbers assuming 67% and 70% turnout. These are its own scenarios, not CIS estimates. [Demócrata](https://www.democrata.es/en/center-of-surveys-and-electoral-polls/general-elections/general-elections-survey-the-recalculation-of-the-cis-places-the-psoe-1-9-points-behind-the-pp-and-gives-194-seats-to-the-pp-and-vox/)
- 2026-10-05: Sánchez called a snap election after Junts, PP and Vox defeated his housing decrees in Congress. The vote comes about 8 months early. [El Salto](https://elsaltodiario.com/estatal/pedro-sanchez-convoca-elecciones-29-noviembre), [Telemundo](https://www.telemundo.com/noticias/noticias-telemundo/internacional/pedro-sanchez-llama-a-elecciones-anticipadas-en-espana-en-medio-de-la-rcna601629)
- I found no published turnout projection or "certain to vote" figure for this election.

## 4. Base rates
- Since 1977 the average is about 72%, and since 2015 the range is 66.2% to 71.8%. The last three elections were 66.48% (2016), 66.23% (Nov 2019) and 66.59% (2023). The 2023 vote was held in July. The other November elections were 68.94% (2011) and 66.23% (2019).
- Change from one election to the next is typically ±1 to 6 points. The big swings (2004, April 2019) came with high polarisation or a mobilising shock.
- CERA turnout was 6.85% in 2019, under the old rule that voters abroad had to request their ballot. It was about 9 to 10% in 2023 after that rule was abolished: 208,451 votes from a CERA census of 2,327,986. [España Exterior PDF](https://www.espanaexterior.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/TABLAS-VOTO-CERA-23J23-©EE.pdf), [Vozpópuli](https://www.vozpopuli.com/opinion/el-caballo-de-troya-de-la-memoria-democratica.html)
- **Composition effect (my own arithmetic):** CERA has grown from about 6.2% of the electorate in 2023 to 7.2% now. Suppose residents vote at the 2023 rate (about 70.4%) and CERA at about 10%. That gives roughly 25.3M + 0.28M ≈ 25.6M votes, or **about 66.1%**. Each point of resident turnout moves the overall figure by about 0.93 points.

## 5. Other forecasts
- **Kalshi** (counts total votes, so check whether CERA votes are included): P(≥25.5M) = 0.73, P(≥26.0M) = 0.61, P(≥26.5M) = 0.45, P(≥27.0M) = 0.29, P(≥27.5M) = 0.19, P(≥28.0M) = 0.10. The median is about 26.4M votes, which is **about 68.2%** of 38.73M. The 26.0M threshold equals 67.1% and 27.0M equals 69.7%.
- **Polymarket** "Spain General Election: Turnout": <62%: 4.4%, 62-64%: 7.5%, 64-66%: 18%, 66-68%: 15.5%, 68-70%: 27%, 70%+: 35.5%. The bins sum to about 105%. The market leans high, which may mean it resolves on the election-night resident-only figure (about 70% in 2023). I could not check its rules. That could make it a poor guide to this question's CERA-inclusive definition.
- I found no Manifold market or expert turnout forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- November 12/13 to 27: official campaign period (my estimate, based on the usual 15-day campaign). The CIS pre-election macro-survey is expected mid-November and may include vote-intention or turnout-likelihood data.
- November 19: postal-vote request deadline. Correos usually publishes request counts, a rough indicator of mobilisation.
- November 29: election night. Interior's provisional count will exclude CERA, so expect a figure several points higher than the one this question resolves on.
- About December 2 to 4: CERA votes counted and final provincial counts. The Junta Electoral Central publishes the official results later, possibly after December 31. The question takes the latest figure published by that date.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** Election day is 29 November 2026, 25 days away. The CERA-inclusive figure that decides this question should be available around 2-4 December, and the final scrutiny follows later in December.

**(b) Latest known value:** The official figure for 23 July 2023 was 66.59%, including CERA voters abroad. Turnout among residents only was about 70.4%.

**(c) If nothing changed:** About 66.3%. This assumes 2023 behaviour, minus about 0.3 points because CERA is now a larger share of the electorate.

**(d) If the current trend continued:** The best signal is pre-election mobilisation. Experts and pollsters mostly expect higher turnout than 2023: resident-only estimates run from 68.4% to 77%. I convert with official ≈ 0.928 × resident + 0.7, which gives roughly 64% to 72% on the official measure, with the centre around 68%.

**(e) Historical variation:** Turnout changes by a median of about 3 points between consecutive elections, with a maximum of about 9. Since 2011 the official figure has stayed between 66.2% and 71.8%.

**(f) Experts and markets:**
- Kalshi's implied median is about 26.4M votes. On the full 38.73M electorate that is about 68.2%. Even on a resident-only basis it implies about 73% resident turnout, which converts to roughly 68% on the official measure.
- Polymarket's median is about 68-69%. It may be measuring the resident-only figure, and if so it points somewhat lower on the official measure.
- Pollsters and analysts:
  - NC Report converts to about 64.2%.
  - Demócrata converts to about 69.4%.
  - Michavila converts to about 71-72%.
- A November date avoids the summer drag that held down 2023, and the election is polarised. Both point to turnout near or above the 2023 level.

**(g) Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** A PP-Vox majority looks so certain that left-wing voters disengage. Bad weather and youth abstention add to this, resident turnout falls to about 67%, and the official figure ends near 63%.
- **High:** A tight late race and strong anti-Vox mobilisation, similar to 2004 or April 2019, push resident turnout to about 77%, giving an official figure near 72-73%.

(d) If the current trend continued: polls and experts point to higher mobilisation than in 2023. This is a snap, polarised election, with a possible PP plus Vox majority mobilising both blocs. Converting the resident-only estimates to the official measure:
